findings.explanation: high confidence.  Witness: An extension 0 -> A -> M -> B -> 0 of modules over Gal(N/k_cyc) with trivial actions on both A and B does not split in general. For g'_{m-1} = g_{m-1} + v with v in A, (T - 1)g'_{m-1} = (T - 1)g_{m-1} since T acts trivially on A, so the non-trivial extension class cannot be eliminated by adding elements of A to g_{m-1} and g_m unless the action was already trivial on M (i.e., C/k_cyc was already abelian). Moreover, the coinvariant module X(\tilde{k})_{Gal(\tilde{k}/k)} is not known to be a free Z_p-module, and the matrix in (32.1) confuses rows and columns for the submodule invariant under the action of Gal(N/k_cyc). Hence, the deduction that such a Gal(N/k_cyc)-submodule H exists is mathematically false, invalidating the proof that C = \tilde{k} and X(\tilde{k}) = 0 in Section 4.2.3 and Proposition 4.2.1, upon which Theorem 1.1.1(II) depends for degree 6 fields when |K| = 0 mod p with dim_{F_p} A(k)/pA(k) <= 1 and a + b != 0 mod p (where Proposition 2.2.1 cannot be used). (Alternative proofs available: None provided for this subcase of Proposition 4.2.1). (Impact: Incomplete proof of Proposition 4.2.1 and Theorem 1.1.1(II)).
